note: Track beat (theory-basics), step 3, on the clap-along tool at level beginner (eighths): counted and tapped, held over a longer round, then clapped into the mic with the click only counting in. The count is written as the tool writes it ("1 & 2 &"). It states its moves (tempo 60 to 100) and mentions no selector.

exercise.title: Eighths on the lane: 1 & 2 &
exercise.why: Eighths put a second note exactly halfway between two clicks, and the lane draws it there, so you can see when your "and" comes too soon.

cells.text:
Press Start below to begin a round of eighths at {{=bpm}}. Count "1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &" aloud, saying "and" for each &, and tap on every word with Space or on the lane.
The numbers land on the click and each "and" falls halfway to the next one. Practice until the taps on "and" turn green as easily as the taps on the numbers.

Press Start below to begin a longer round of eighths, and keep counting aloud to the end.
When the round ends, read the line under the numbers: it says whether your taps came early or late on average. Early means the "and" taps are leaning towards the next click, so give each "and" its full half of the beat.

Now clap the eighths. Press Start below to open the mic: the metronome counts one bar in and then stops, so the mic hears only your claps. Clap as each note reaches the line, and keep the count going in your head.
If the claps drift, count aloud again and let every number pull you back onto the beat.
